title: Vernalis on I-5: Exit 449 and Highway 33 Access
meta: Vernalis sits east of I-5 at exit 449 in San Joaquin County, with nearby exits, the I-580 junction and the closest rest areas on the route.
intro: Highway 33 leads to Vernalis, east of the freeway, and its name is Latin for springlike. I-5 Buddy places Vernalis at exit 449, on flat San Joaquin County farmland near the edge of the Delta, between the San Joaquin River and the old railroad towns of Banta and Tracy.

faq.q: What exit is Vernalis on I-5?
faq.a: Vernalis is at exit 449 in I-5 Buddy's data. The listed exits nearby include exit 452 for CA 33 South; Vernalis, and exits 449A and 449B for CA 132.

faq.q: How did Vernalis get its name?
faq.a: The name is Latin for springlike. Local historian Earle Williams said it was named after two ranchers' daughters, Verna Carpenter and Alice Hamilton.

faq.q: Where is the nearest rest area to Vernalis on I-5?
faq.a: Going south, the Westley Rest Area is at mile 444.9, 3.8 miles from Vernalis, and serves both directions. Going north, the Elkhorn Rest Area is at mile 529.3, 80.6 miles from here.

faq.q: What is near Vernalis on I-5?
faq.a: The I-580 junction at exit 446 heads for the Bay Area over Altamont Pass. East of the freeway at exit 449, on the right going north, San Joaquin River National Wildlife Refuge protects more than 7,000 acres of river woodland, wetlands and grassland.
